historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr, cross-checked against the company's own underlying-profit growth (+7% FY2024->FY2025, excluding one-off items) and near-flat FY2020-2025 revenue CAGR (~1.0%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported EPS/net-income CAGR (-15% to -31%) diverges sharply from revenue and equity CAGRs (~1-2%) but is a false signal: FY2025 net income was cut by a HK$10,469m NON-CASH UK-merger loss and FY2024 by a HK$3,740m non-cash Vietnam-telecom impairment, neither of which touches cash flow or FCF (FCF CAGR 3yr +10%, 5yr roughly flat). Growth rate is anchored on revenue/equity/underlying-profit, not on the impairment-distorted reported-EPS series.

scenario_narratives.base: Flat-to-low-single-digit organic growth across a diversified five-segment portfolio, margin held near the current ~27% level (no assumed recovery to the pre-2022 ~35-38% mix), cash tax drifting to ~21%. The Panama concession loss is already excluded from the base (occurred Feb-2026, prior to this valuation). Balance sheet materially de-levered by the UK Power Networks disposal (net debt down from HK$113.7bn at FY2025 to HK$67.5bn at H1 FY2026) -- captured in the anchor, not projected as a repeatable FCF driver.
scenario_narratives.bull: A.S. Watson IPO crystallises retail value on schedule, VodafoneThree and Cenovus outperform, the stalled global ports consortium sale eventually completes at full value.
scenario_narratives.bear: Geopolitical/national-security risk to ports and telecom concessions resurfaces beyond Panama, the ports consortium sale stays stalled, European telecom stays low-return, and the A.S. Watson IPO catalyst slips or disappoints -- growth stalls and margin compresses on structural retail mix shift.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CK Hutchison is valued as a going, cash-generative diversified conglomerate on its consolidated owner-FCF, not as a pure listed-investment holdco (no NAV/exit-discount model) and not as a pure look-through JV stake (unlike IGO.AX). The Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows already nets in cash dividends actually received from equity-accounted associates/JVs (ports/infrastructure/telecom stakes held that way) while excluding their non-cash equity-pickup profit share, so building the DCF on reported consolidated FCF captures the whole portfolio's real cash contribution without double-counting. SBC is genuinely zero (no share scheme exists). Leases are treated as debt (treatment A): lease principal already sits outside OCF/FCF (financing activities), so lease liabilities are added to net debt in the equity bridge rather than charged again through the flows. The Panama ports concession loss (Feb-2026) is already excluded from the base-year anchors; the pending arbitration claim is a memo-only, uncapitalized contingent upside. Net debt is anchored to the LATEST (30-Jun-2026) balance sheet, which is materially lower than 31-Dec-2025 following the GBP10.5bn UK Power Networks disposal completing 7-May-2026 -- a real, durable balance-sheet improvement, not a flow item projected forward.
key_risks_to_valuation: Further concession/regulatory losses beyond Panama (ports and telecom are increasingly treated as critical national-security assets globally)
The non-Panama global ports consortium sale (BlackRock/MSC/COSCO, ~US$22.8bn) stays stalled indefinitely or falls through, removing an expected value-crystallisation event
A.S. Watson's dual-listing IPO (targeted ~US$30bn) slips further (already flagged to 2027) or prices materially below target
Structural retail margin compression (A.S. Watson ~9% EBITDA margin segment, 41% of segment revenue) drags the consolidated blended margin below the ~27% base assumption
European telecom remains a low-return, capital-intensive, price-competitive industry despite VodafoneThree in-market consolidation

Complex proportionate-consolidation/equity-accounting structure makes the true look-through economics harder to verify than a simple consolidated peer -- the FCF-based approach here relies on the dividends-received line remaining a reasonable proxy for the JV/associate cash contribution over the forecast horizon

inputs.sbc_source: Company and subsidiaries have no share option or share award scheme (FY2025 Annual Report note 10.503/14.410-14.413: 'neither the Company nor its subsidiary companies had a share option scheme'); genuinely SBC-zero, not undisclosed
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T08:08:12Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, HKD)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% built on HKD/HK risk-free (HK long bond tracks USD given the peg, ~4.0-4.3%) plus an equity risk premium of ~4.5-5.0pp reflecting a mature, geographically diversified but geopolitically-exposed multi-segment conglomerate (Panama concession loss, national-security scrutiny on ports/telecom). No per-scenario WACC variation -- risk is charged in the scenario cash flows (Panama/consortium-sale/trade-slowdown assumptions differ by scenario), not stacked again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) -- leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease PRINCIPAL sits in financing activities on the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows (FY2025: HK$14,839m, note 34(e)) and is never inside 'Net cash from operating activities' (HK$62,567m), so reported OCF/FCF is not flattered by lease principal already. Lease INTEREST is inside 'Interest expenses and other finance costs paid (net)' within operating activities, so it is already charged in the flows. Lease liabilities (H1 FY2026: HK$12,787m current + HK$50,705m non-current = HK$63,492m) are EXCLUDED from the company's own 'Net debt' definition (FY2025 Annual Report note 4: 'Total bank and other debts less total cash, liquid funds and other listed investments') -- added separately in the equity bridge below so they are charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are attributable-only: 'last_fcf'/'reported_fcf' derive from the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows, which is prepared net of non-controlling interests' and perpetual-capital-securities holders' claims on profit (the P&L already deducts 'Profit attributable to non-controlling interests and holders of perpetual capital securities' of HK$7,529m FY2025 before arriving at 'Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders'; OCF is built off consolidated pre-tax cash generation net of minority cash calls via dividends paid to NCI in financing, not double-subtracted in the DCF). No separate NCI deduction is taken in the bridge -- would double-count.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md to the owner-FCF DCF (component route) + owner-fcf-adaptations.md, NOT a pure sum-of-parts/NAV holdco model. CKHH is a genuinely consolidated operating conglomerate -- it publishes one Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows that is the real cash the parent controls, not a listed-investment holding company holding only tradeable stakes (contrast AFIC/BIT/TEM, which get NAV+exit-discount). Ports and retail (A.S. Watson) are substantially consolidated subsidiaries; infrastructure (CKI) and much of telecom are equity-accounted associates/JVs whose PROFIT SHARE is excluded from consolidated EBITDA/D&A/capex but whose CASH DIVIDENDS (HK$12,303m FY2025, per note 34(a)) flow through 'Net cash from operating activities' -- this is exactly the cash CKHH can distribute, so building the DCF on the reported consolidated FCF series captures the JV/associate contribution correctly without double-counting their non-cash equity pickup. This mirrors the IGO.AX 'look-through JV' problem but resolved the other way: unlike IGO (which becomes ~100% one JV stake), CKHH's consolidated statement already captures a large, diversified, going operating business directly, so no separate look-through build was needed -- the consolidated cash-flow statement IS the right base. SBC-ZERO market (band_position set to null; house and street coincide -- see adaptations.md section (e)). NORMALIZATION: H1 FY2026 reported net income HK$26,801m is flattered by ~HK$16.7bn 'other income and gains' (mostly UK Power Networks and UK Rail disposal gains) and is NOT used as a run-rate. Base-year FCF (HK$43,824m FY2025) is used as-is because FCF (unlike net income) is not distorted by disposal-gain P&L noise in FY2025 -- the FY2025 FCF print is close to the FY2023-2025 3-year average (HK$35,818m) and the underlying-profit-basis trend (see below), so no further mid-cycle adjustment to the cash-flow base was applied beyond anchoring growth to the company's own UK-Telecom-excluding underlying profit trend rather than reported net income. Reported net income swung -31% FY2025 (UK merger non-cash loss HK$10,469m) and -16% FY2024 (Vietnam telecom impairment HK$3,740m) -- neither is a cash item and neither is in the FCF base, confirming FCF is the right growth anchor, not EPS/NI. Company's own 'Underlying Profit Attributable to Ordinary Shareholder' (excludes one-off items) grew HK$20,828m FY2024 -> HK$22,310m FY2025, +7% -- used to calibrate base-case growth given flat headline revenue (FY2020-2025 revenue CAGR ~1.0%, equity CAGR ~1.8%). NET DEBT: used the company's own reported 'Net debt' (bank/other debt less cash & liquid investments, excludes lease liabilities per its own Note 4 definition) at the LATEST balance-sheet date (30-Jun-2026: HK$67,510m, down sharply from HK$113,692m at 31-Dec-2025 following the UK Power Networks disposal completing 7-May-2026 for GBP10.5bn) rather than core_metrics.total_debt/cash (which appear stale/inconsistent with the FY2025 10-K's own 'total bank and other debts' of HK$265,002m -- core_metrics.total_debt of HK$330,089m does not reconcile and was not used). PANAMA: the Panama Ports concession (Balboa/Cristobal) was annulled Feb-2026 and is already OUT of the Group's operations and cash flows by the valuation date -- the FY2025/H1-2026 base already excludes it; no further deduction needed, but the pending arbitration claim (~US$1.5-2bn) is a memo-only contingent upside NOT capitalized into any scenario (too uncertain to value).

bear.narrative: Continued national-security/geopolitical scrutiny of ports and telecom (Panama-style concession risk resurfaces elsewhere), the non-Panama global ports consortium sale stays stalled indefinitely denying value crystallisation, global trade growth slows further pressuring ports throughput, European telecom stays a low-return, capital-intensive, price-competitive industry limiting VodafoneThree synergy realisation, and A.S. Watson's IPO slips repeatedly (now flagged to 2027) or prices well below the targeted ~US$30bn, denying the value-crystallisation catalyst. Retail margins compress further under e-commerce and cost pressure, consistent with the segment's structurally thin ~9% EBITDA margin. Risk is charged in these flows, not by raising WACC above base -- a single flat 8.5% WACC is used across scenarios per the house rule against charging risk twice.

base.narrative: Mature, geographically-diversified conglomerate compounding low-single-digit organic revenue (retail/A.S. Watson and telecom grow modestly, ports benefit from trade-route diversification, infrastructure stable/regulated) after the Panama concession loss is already out of the base. Margin holds roughly flat near the current 27% consolidated EBITDA margin -- no assumed recovery of the pre-2022 ~35-38% level, reflecting the structural mix shift toward lower-margin retail. Cash tax rate continues its recent rise toward a ~21% blended rate. Capital recycling (UK Power Networks completed, A.S. Watson IPO targeted but not modeled as a discrete event) is a balance-sheet/net-debt tailwind already reflected in the much-reduced H1 FY2026 net debt anchor, not in the FCF growth path.

bull.narrative: A.S. Watson's dual HK/London IPO (targeting ~US$30bn valuation) proceeds and lands on schedule, crystallising retail value and funding growth/buybacks; VodafoneThree synergies and European telecom in-market consolidation lift telecom margins faster than base case; Cenovus (post-MEG Energy) and other Finance & Investments associates deliver stronger commodity-price-driven contributions; the stalled non-Panama global ports consortium sale (BlackRock/MSC/COSCO) eventually completes at a full price, crystallising further value and de-risking the geopolitical overhang; successful Panama arbitration recovery is a memo-only upside not included in these cash flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because CKHH carries multiple LIVE, unresolved, binary-ish geopolitical/regulatory risks concentrated in headline assets (the stalled US$22.8bn non-Panama ports consortium sale amid US-China tensions, national-security scrutiny extending beyond the already-realised Panama loss, and a European telecom industry that remains structurally low-return even after VodafoneThree). Bull weight trimmed to 25% because it requires several largely independent things to go right (A.S. Watson IPO landing on schedule at the targeted valuation, the ports consortium sale completing, AND Cenovus/telecom outperformance) -- a bull case needing multiple correlated wins gets less weight per the house rule. Base at 45% (below the 50% default) reflects that this is a genuinely three-way-uncertain situation rather than a business with one dominant, highly-likely path.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
